title: Liberty-Fever takeaways: Kelsey Mitchell drops 33 points, Clark picks up sixth technical
content:
INDIANAPOLIS — After recording a franchise-record 45 points and 10 assists in a comeback win over the Seattle Storm on Friday, Indiana Fever guard Caitlin Clark came back down to earth Saturday in the Fever’s 108-88 victory over the New York Liberty.

Clark finished with 17 points and seven assists, while teammate Kelsey Mitchell paced the team with a game-high 33 points. The Fever notched their second straight win and fourth in five games. The Liberty, meanwhile, have lost four straight.

Clark’s participation in Friday’s and Saturday’s games marked her first back-to-back in over two years. Until this week, she hadn’t played in a back-to-back since 2024, her rookie season, after being limited to 13 games last year due to various injuries and managing persistent back issues this year.

Clark finally took a significant step forward in her health by suiting up Saturday, just over 24 hours after becoming the 11th player in WNBA history to score 45 points in a game. The three-time All-Star provided a few highlights, including two and-1s in the second half, but shot just 5-for-14 from the field and 2-for-8 on 3s. She also coughed up seven turnovers.

Mitchell kept the Fever’s offense humming. The four-time All-Star scored 14 points in the third quarter as Indiana outscored the Liberty 30-12 in the frame to take a 14-point lead into the fourth quarter. Mitchell provided arguably the play of the game when she drilled a pull-up 3-pointer while being fouled by the Liberty’s Breanna Stewart with just under four minutes left in the game. The 4-point play gave Mitchell her fourth 30-point game of the season and extended her franchise record to 15 30-point outings.

Aliyah Boston, also a four-time All-Star, returned from a one-game absence due to a lower right leg injury and chipped in with 15 points, seven rebounds and four assists in 24 minutes. Sophie Cunningham added 11 points off the bench, punctuated by three 3s.

The Liberty, viewed as a perennial contender in recent years, have lost eight of their last 10 games (excluding their victory in the Commissioners’ Cup championship, which does not count toward their regular-season record).

New York built a 13-point lead in the second quarter, but the Fever cut that lead to 4 at halftime. The Liberty were unable to find much offensive success after the break. Stewart poured in a team-high 26 points on 10-for-16 shooting, but she missed five of her nine free-throw attempts. Jonquel Jones and Sabrina Ionescu were limited to just 13 and 12 points, respectively.

To compound their troubles, Liberty guard Marine Johannes left the game in the fourth quarter with what appeared to be a left ankle injury after she stepped on the foot of Fever guard Tyasha Harris. She grimaced as she was helped back to the locker room, flanked by a teammate and trainer. Johannes scored all 12 of her points in the first quarter and played 18 minutes.

Clark was assessed a technical foul in the first quarter of Saturday’s game and now has six technical fouls on the season. If she reaches eight, she’ll receive a WNBA-mandated one-game suspension.

Clark picked up a technical foul after she was leveled on a screen by Jones. The play was a no-call, but Clark took exception to the physicality and yelled at the closest official. Liberty star Breanna Stewart drained the ensuing technical foul free throw to give New York a 9-2 lead with 8:29 left in the first quarter.

Earlier this season, Clark said she wouldn’t change her approach after she picked up her fifth technical foul last month in a win over the Phoenix Mercury. In that contest, Clark was assessed a technical foul for loudly clapping in the direction of Mercury players during a skirmish, which Fever coach Stephanie White said the officials deemed as taunting.

“We should all just go on the calendar now and pick a game that I’m gonna be suspended for if I’m gonna get technicals for clapping,” Clark said after that game.

The Fever have previously appealed Clark’s technical fouls, but if this one is not rescinded, she’ll be tied with Mercury guard Kahleah Copper for the second-most technical fouls in the WNBA this season. Atlanta Dream forward Angel Reese leads the league with seven technical fouls.
